134 VariableInfo{S,T,U,V}

141 struct VariableInfo{S,T,U,V}
142 has_lb::Bool
143 lower_bound::S
144 has_ub::Bool
145 upper_bound::T
146 has_fix::Bool
147 fixed_value::U
148 has_start::Bool
149 start::V
150 binary::Bool
151 integer::Bool
152 function VariableInfo(
153 has_lb::Bool,
154 lower_bound::S,
155 has_ub::Bool,
156 upper_bound::T,
157 has_fix::Bool,
158 fixed_value::U,
159 has_start::Bool,
160 start::V,
161 binary::Bool,
162 integer::Bool,
163 ) where {S,T,U,V}
164 if has_lb && !_isfinite(lower_bound)
165 has_lb = false
166 lower_bound = NaN
167 end
168 if has_ub && !_isfinite(upper_bound)
169 has_ub = false
170 upper_bound = NaN
171 end
172 if has_fix && !_isfinite(fixed_value)
173 error("Unable to fix variable to $(fixed_value)")
174 end
175 return new{typeof(lower_bound),typeof(upper_bound),U,V}(
176 has_lb,
177 lower_bound,
178 has_ub,
179 upper_bound,
180 has_fix,
181 fixed_value,
182 has_start,
183 start,
184 binary,
185 integer,
186 )
187 end
188 end

304 function Base.showerror(io::IO, err::VariableNotOwned)
305 return print(
306 io,
307 """
308 $err: the variable $(err.variable) cannot be used in this model because
309 it belongs to a different model.
310
311 ## Explanation
312
313 Each variable belongs to a particular model. You cannot use a variable
314 inside a model to which it does not belong. For example:
315
316 ```julia
317 model = Model()
318 @variable(model, x >= 0)
319 model2 = Model()
320 @objective(model2, Min, x) # Errors because x belongs to `model`
321 ```
322
323 One common cause of this error is working with a main problem and a
324 subproblem.
325
326 ```julia
327 model = Model()
328 @variable(model, x, Bin)
329 subproblem = Model()
330 @variable(subproblem, 0 <= x <= 1)
331 # The Julia binding `x` now refers to `subproblem[:x]`, not `model[:x]`
332 @objective(model, Min, x) # Errors because x belongs to `subproblem`
333 # do instead
334 @objective(model, Min, model[:x])
335 ```""",
336 )
337 end

443 """
444 delete(model::GenericModel, variable_ref::GenericVariableRef)
445
446 Delete the variable associated with `variable_ref` from the model `model`.
447
448 Note that `delete` does not unregister the name from the model, so adding a new
449 variable of the same name will throw an error. Use [`unregister`](@ref) to
450 unregister the name after deletion.
451
452 ## Example
453
454 ```jldoctest
455 julia> model = Model();
456
457 julia> @variable(model, x)
458 x
459
460 julia> delete(model, x)
461
462 julia> unregister(model, :x)
463
464 julia> print(model)
465 Feasibility
466 Subject to
467
468 julia> model[:x]
469 ERROR: KeyError: key :x not found
470 Stacktrace:
471 [...]
472 ```
473 """
474 function delete(model::GenericModel, variable_ref::GenericVariableRef)
475 if model !== owner_model(variable_ref)
476 error(
477 "The variable reference you are trying to delete does not " *
478 "belong to the model.",
479 )
480 end
481 model.is_model_dirty = true
482 MOI.delete(backend(model), variable_ref.index)
483 return
484 end
485
486 """
487 delete(model::GenericModel, variable_refs::Vector{<:GenericVariableRef})
488
489 Delete the variables associated with `variable_refs` from the model `model`.
490 Solvers may implement methods for deleting multiple variables that are
491 more efficient than repeatedly calling the single variable delete method.
492
493 See also: [`unregister`](@ref)
494
495 ## Example
496
497 ```jldoctest
498 julia> model = Model();
499
500 julia> @variable(model, x[1:2]);
501
502 julia> delete(model, x)
503
504 julia> unregister(model, :x)
505
506 julia> print(model)
507 Feasibility
508 Subject to
509
510 julia> model[:x]
511 ERROR: KeyError: key :x not found
512 Stacktrace:
513 [...]
514 ```
515 """
516 function delete(
517 model::GenericModel,
518 variable_refs::Vector{<:GenericVariableRef},
519 )
520 if any(model !== owner_model(v) for v in variable_refs)
521 error(
522 "A variable reference you are trying to delete does not " *
523 "belong to the model.",
524 )
525 end
526 model.is_model_dirty = true
527 MOI.delete(backend(model), index.(variable_refs))
528 return
529 end

792 """
793 has_lower_bound(v::GenericVariableRef)
794
795 Return `true` if `v` has a lower bound. If `true`, the lower bound can be
796 queried with [`lower_bound`](@ref).
797
798 See also [`LowerBoundRef`](@ref), [`lower_bound`](@ref),
799 [`set_lower_bound`](@ref), [`delete_lower_bound`](@ref).
800
801 ## Example
802
803 ```jldoctest
804 julia> model = Model();
805
806 julia> @variable(model, x >= 1.0);
807
808 julia> has_lower_bound(x)
809 true
810 ```
811 """
812 function has_lower_bound(v::GenericVariableRef)
813 return _moi_has_lower_bound(backend(owner_model(v)), v)
814 end
815
816 # _moi_* methods allow us to work around the type instability of the backend of
817 # a model.
818 function _moi_has_lower_bound(moi_backend, v::GenericVariableRef)
819 return MOI.is_valid(moi_backend, _lower_bound_index(v))
820 end
821
822 function _lower_bound_index(v::GenericVariableRef{T}) where {T}
823 return MOI.ConstraintIndex{MOI.VariableIndex,MOI.GreaterThan{T}}(
824 index(v).value,
825 )
826 end
827
828 """
829 set_lower_bound(v::GenericVariableRef, lower::Number)
830
831 Set the lower bound of a variable. If one does not exist, create a new lower
832 bound constraint.
833
834 See also [`LowerBoundRef`](@ref), [`has_lower_bound`](@ref),
835 [`lower_bound`](@ref), [`delete_lower_bound`](@ref).
836
837 ## Example
838
839 ```jldoctest
840 julia> model = Model();
841
842 julia> @variable(model, x >= 1.0);
843
844 julia> lower_bound(x)
845 1.0
846
847 julia> set_lower_bound(x, 2.0)
848
849 julia> lower_bound(x)
850 2.0
851 ```
852 """
853 function set_lower_bound(v::GenericVariableRef, lower::Number)
854 if !isfinite(lower)
855 error(
856 "Unable to set lower bound to $(lower). To remove the bound, use " *
857 "`delete_lower_bound`.",
858 )
859 end
860 model = owner_model(v)
861 model.is_model_dirty = true
862 _moi_set_lower_bound(backend(model), v, lower)
863 return
864 end
865
866 function _moi_set_lower_bound(
867 moi_backend,
868 v::GenericVariableRef{T},
869 lower::Number,
870 ) where {T}
871 new_set = MOI.GreaterThan(convert(T, lower))
872 if _moi_has_lower_bound(moi_backend, v)
873 cindex = _lower_bound_index(v)
874 MOI.set(moi_backend, MOI.ConstraintSet(), cindex, new_set)
875 else
876 @assert !_moi_is_fixed(moi_backend, v)
877 _moi_add_constraint(moi_backend, index(v), new_set)
878 end
879 return
880 end
881
882 """
883 LowerBoundRef(v::GenericVariableRef)
884
885 Return a constraint reference to the lower bound constraint of `v`.
886
887 Errors if one does not exist.
888
889 See also [`has_lower_bound`](@ref), [`lower_bound`](@ref),
890 [`set_lower_bound`](@ref), [`delete_lower_bound`](@ref).
891
892 ## Example
893
894 ```jldoctest
895 julia> model = Model();
896
897 julia> @variable(model, x >= 1.0);
898
899 julia> LowerBoundRef(x)
900 x ≥ 1
901 ```
902 """
903 function LowerBoundRef(v::GenericVariableRef)
904 if !has_lower_bound(v)
905 error("Variable $(v) does not have a lower bound.")
906 end
907 return ConstraintRef(owner_model(v), _lower_bound_index(v), ScalarShape())
908 end
909
910 """
911 delete_lower_bound(v::GenericVariableRef)
912
913 Delete the lower bound constraint of a variable.
914
915 See also [`LowerBoundRef`](@ref), [`has_lower_bound`](@ref),
916 [`lower_bound`](@ref), [`set_lower_bound`](@ref).
917
918 ## Example
919
920 ```jldoctest
921 julia> model = Model();
922
923 julia> @variable(model, x >= 1.0);
924
925 julia> has_lower_bound(x)
926 true
927
928 julia> delete_lower_bound(x)
929
930 julia> has_lower_bound(x)
931 false
932 ```
933 """
934 function delete_lower_bound(variable_ref::GenericVariableRef)
935 delete(owner_model(variable_ref), LowerBoundRef(variable_ref))
936 return
937 end
938
939 """
940 lower_bound(v::GenericVariableRef)
941
942 Return the lower bound of a variable. Error if one does not exist.
943
944 See also [`LowerBoundRef`](@ref), [`has_lower_bound`](@ref),
945 [`set_lower_bound`](@ref), [`delete_lower_bound`](@ref).
946
947 ## Example
948
949 ```jldoctest
950 julia> model = Model();
951
952 julia> @variable(model, x >= 1.0);
953
954 julia> lower_bound(x)
955 1.0
956 ```
957 """
958 function lower_bound(v::GenericVariableRef{T}) where {T}
959 set = MOI.get(owner_model(v), MOI.ConstraintSet(), LowerBoundRef(v))
960 return set.lower::T
961 end

1047 @assert !_moi_is_fixed(moi_backend, v)

1137
1138 # MOI.EqualTo
1139
1140 """
1141 is_fixed(v::GenericVariableRef)
1142
1143 Return `true` if `v` is a fixed variable. If `true`, the fixed value can be
1144 queried with [`fix_value`](@ref).
1145
1146 See also [`FixRef`](@ref), [`fix_value`](@ref), [`fix`](@ref), [`unfix`](@ref).
1147
1148 ## Example
1149
1150 ```jldoctest
1151 julia> model = Model();
1152
1153 julia> @variable(model, x);
1154
1155 julia> is_fixed(x)
1156 false
1157
1158 julia> fix(x, 1.0)
1159
1160 julia> is_fixed(x)
1161 true
1162 ```
1163 """
1164 function is_fixed(v::GenericVariableRef)
1165 return _moi_is_fixed(backend(owner_model(v)), v)
1166 end
1167
1168 function _moi_is_fixed(moi_backend, v::GenericVariableRef)
1169 return MOI.is_valid(moi_backend, _fix_index(v))
1170 end
1171
1172 function _fix_index(v::GenericVariableRef{T}) where {T}
1173 return MOI.ConstraintIndex{MOI.VariableIndex,MOI.EqualTo{T}}(index(v).value)
1174 end
1175
1176 """
1177 fix(v::GenericVariableRef, value::Number; force::Bool = false)
1178
1179 Fix a variable to a value. Update the fixing constraint if one exists, otherwise
1180 create a new one.
1181
1182 If the variable already has variable bounds and `force=false`, calling `fix`
1183 will throw an error. If `force=true`, existing variable bounds will be deleted,
1184 and the fixing constraint will be added. Note a variable will have no bounds
1185 after a call to [`unfix`](@ref).
1186
1187 See also [`FixRef`](@ref), [`is_fixed`](@ref), [`fix_value`](@ref),
1188 [`unfix`](@ref).
1189
1190 ## Example
1191
1192 ```jldoctest
1193 julia> model = Model();
1194
1195 julia> @variable(model, x);
1196
1197 julia> is_fixed(x)
1198 false
1199
1200 julia> fix(x, 1.0)
1201
1202 julia> is_fixed(x)
1203 true
1204 ```
1205
1206 ```jldoctest
1207 julia> model = Model();
1208
1209 julia> @variable(model, 0 <= x <= 1);
1210
1211 julia> is_fixed(x)
1212 false
1213
1214 julia> fix(x, 1.0; force = true)
1215
1216 julia> is_fixed(x)
1217 true
1218 ```
1219 """
1220 function fix(variable::GenericVariableRef, value::Number; force::Bool = false)
1221 if !isfinite(value)
1222 error("Unable to fix variable to $(value)")
1223 end
1224 model = owner_model(variable)
1225 model.is_model_dirty = true
1226 _moi_fix(backend(model), variable, value, force)
1227 return
1228 end
1229
1230 function _moi_fix(
1231 moi_backend,
1232 variable::GenericVariableRef{T},
1233 value::Number,
1234 force::Bool,
1235 ) where {T}
1236 new_set = MOI.EqualTo(convert(T, value))
1237 if _moi_is_fixed(moi_backend, variable) # Update existing fixing constraint.
1238 c_index = _fix_index(variable)
1239 MOI.set(moi_backend, MOI.ConstraintSet(), c_index, new_set)
1240 else # Add a new fixing constraint.
1241 if _moi_has_upper_bound(moi_backend, variable) ||
1242 _moi_has_lower_bound(moi_backend, variable)
1243 if !force
1244 error(
1245 "Unable to fix $(variable) to $(value) because it has " *
1246 "existing variable bounds. Consider calling " *
1247 "`JuMP.fix(variable, value; force=true)` which will " *
1248 "delete existing bounds before fixing the variable.",
1249 )
1250 end
1251 if _moi_has_upper_bound(moi_backend, variable)
1252 MOI.delete(moi_backend, _upper_bound_index(variable))
1253 end
1254 if _moi_has_lower_bound(moi_backend, variable)
1255 MOI.delete(moi_backend, _lower_bound_index(variable))
1256 end
1257 end
1258 _moi_add_constraint(moi_backend, index(variable), new_set)
1259 end
1260 return
1261 end
1262
1263 """
1264 unfix(v::GenericVariableRef)
1265
1266 Delete the fixing constraint of a variable.
1267
1268 Error if one does not exist.
1269
1270 See also [`FixRef`](@ref), [`is_fixed`](@ref), [`fix_value`](@ref),
1271 [`fix`](@ref).
1272
1273 ## Example
1274
1275 ```jldoctest
1276 julia> model = Model();
1277
1278 julia> @variable(model, x == 1);
1279
1280 julia> is_fixed(x)
1281 true
1282
1283 julia> unfix(x)
1284
1285 julia> is_fixed(x)
1286 false
1287 ```
1288 """
1289 function unfix(variable_ref::GenericVariableRef)
1290 delete(owner_model(variable_ref), FixRef(variable_ref))
1291 return
1292 end
1293
1294 """
1295 fix_value(v::GenericVariableRef)
1296
1297 Return the value to which a variable is fixed.
1298
1299 Error if one does not exist.
1300
1301 See also [`FixRef`](@ref), [`is_fixed`](@ref), [`fix`](@ref), [`unfix`](@ref).
1302
1303 ## Example
1304
1305 ```jldoctest
1306 julia> model = Model();
1307
1308 julia> @variable(model, x == 1);
1309
1310 julia> fix_value(x)
1311 1.0
1312 ```
1313 """
1314 function fix_value(v::GenericVariableRef{T}) where {T}
1315 set = MOI.get(owner_model(v), MOI.ConstraintSet(), FixRef(v))
1316 return set.value::T
1317 end
1318
1319 """
1320 FixRef(v::GenericVariableRef)
1321
1322 Return a constraint reference to the constraint fixing the value of `v`.
1323
1324 Errors if one does not exist.
1325
1326 See also [`is_fixed`](@ref), [`fix_value`](@ref), [`fix`](@ref),
1327 [`unfix`](@ref).
1328
1329 ## Example
1330
1331 ```jldoctest
1332 julia> model = Model();
1333
1334 julia> @variable(model, x == 1);
1335
1336 julia> FixRef(x)
1337 x = 1
1338 ```
1339 """
1340 function FixRef(v::GenericVariableRef)
1341 if !is_fixed(v)
1342 error("Variable $(v) does not have fixed bounds.")
1343 end
1344 return ConstraintRef(owner_model(v), _fix_index(v), ScalarShape())
1345 end

1347 # MOI.Integer
1348
1349 """
1350 is_integer(v::GenericVariableRef)
1351
1352 Return `true` if `v` is constrained to be integer.
1353
1354 See also [`IntegerRef`](@ref), [`set_integer`](@ref), [`unset_integer`](@ref).
1355
1356 ## Example
1357
1358 ```jldoctest
1359 julia> model = Model();
1360
1361 julia> @variable(model, x);
1362
1363 julia> is_integer(x)
1364 false
1365
1366 julia> set_integer(x)
1367
1368 julia> is_integer(x)
1369 true
1370 ```
1371 """
1372 function is_integer(v::GenericVariableRef)
1373 return _moi_is_integer(backend(owner_model(v)), v)
1374 end
1375
1376 function _moi_is_integer(moi_backend, v::GenericVariableRef)
1377 return MOI.is_valid(moi_backend, _integer_index(v))
1378 end
1379
1380 function _integer_index(v::GenericVariableRef)
1381 return MOI.ConstraintIndex{MOI.VariableIndex,MOI.Integer}(index(v).value)
1382 end
1383
1384 """
1385 set_integer(variable_ref::GenericVariableRef)
1386
1387 Add an integrality constraint on the variable `variable_ref`.
1388
1389 See also [`IntegerRef`](@ref), [`is_integer`](@ref), [`unset_integer`](@ref).
1390
1391 ## Example
1392
1393 ```jldoctest
1394 julia> model = Model();
1395
1396 julia> @variable(model, x);
1397
1398 julia> is_integer(x)
1399 false
1400
1401 julia> set_integer(x)
1402
1403 julia> is_integer(x)
1404 true
1405 ```
1406 """
1407 function set_integer(v::GenericVariableRef)
1408 model = owner_model(v)
1409 model.is_model_dirty = true
1410 _moi_set_integer(backend(model), v)
1411 return
1412 end
1413
1414 function _moi_set_integer(moi_backend, variable_ref::GenericVariableRef)
1415 if _moi_is_integer(moi_backend, variable_ref)
1416 return
1417 elseif _moi_is_binary(moi_backend, variable_ref)
1418 error(
1419 "Cannot set the variable_ref $(variable_ref) to integer as it " *
1420 "is already binary.",
1421 )
1422 end
1423 _moi_add_constraint(moi_backend, index(variable_ref), MOI.Integer())
1424 return
1425 end
1426
1427 """
1428 unset_integer(variable_ref::GenericVariableRef)
1429
1430 Remove the integrality constraint on the variable `variable_ref`.

1432 Errors if one does not exist.

1438 ```jldoctest
1439 julia> model = Model();
1440
1441 julia> @variable(model, x, Int);
1442
1443 julia> is_integer(x)
1444 true
1445
1446 julia> unset_integer(x)
1447
1448 julia> is_integer(x)
1449 false
1450 ```
1451 """
1452 function unset_integer(variable_ref::GenericVariableRef)
1453 delete(owner_model(variable_ref), IntegerRef(variable_ref))
1454 return
1455 end

1458 IntegerRef(v::GenericVariableRef)
1459
1460 Return a constraint reference to the constraint constraining `v` to be integer.

1462 Errors if one does not exist.

1629 ```jldoctest
1630 julia> model = Model();
1631
1632 julia> @variable(model, p in Parameter(2))
1633 p
1634
1635 julia> ParameterRef(p)

1637
1638 julia> @variable(model, x);
1639
1640 julia> ParameterRef(x)
1641 ERROR: Variable x is not a parameter.
1642 Stacktrace:
1643 [...]
1644 ```
1645 """
1646 function ParameterRef(x::GenericVariableRef)
1647 if !is_parameter(x)
1648 error("Variable $x is not a parameter.")
1649 end
1650 return ConstraintRef(owner_model(x), _parameter_index(x), ScalarShape())
1651 end
1652
1653 function _parameter_index(x::GenericVariableRef)
1654 F, S = MOI.VariableIndex, MOI.Parameter{value_type(typeof(x))}
1655 return MOI.ConstraintIndex{F,S}(index(x).value)
1656 end

1658 """
1659 is_parameter(x::GenericVariableRef)::Bool

1664 [`parameter_value`](@ref).

1668 ```jldoctest
1669 julia> model = Model();
1670
1671 julia> @variable(model, p in Parameter(2))
1672 p

1674 julia> is_parameter(p)

1676
1677 julia> @variable(model, x)
1678 x
1679
1680 julia> is_parameter(x)

1684 function is_parameter(x::GenericVariableRef)
1685 return MOI.is_valid(backend(owner_model(x)), _parameter_index(x))::Bool

1688 """
1689 set_parameter_value(x::GenericVariableRef, value)
1690
1691 Update the parameter constraint on the variable `x` to `value`.

1693 Errors if `x` is not a parameter.

1710
1711 julia> parameter_value(p)

1715 function set_parameter_value(x::GenericVariableRef, value)
1716 model = owner_model(x)

1718 model.is_model_dirty = true

1720 MOI.set(model, MOI.ConstraintSet(), ParameterRef(x), set)
1721 return
1722 end

1762 """
1763 is_variable_in_set(
1764 model::GenericModel,
1765 x::Union{AbstractJuMPScalar,AbstractArray{<:AbstractJuMPScalar}},
1766 )::Bool
1767
1768 Return a `Bool` if [`VariableInSetRef`](@ref) returns a valid constraint
1769 reference without erroring.
1770
1771 ## Exceptions
1772
1773 This function does not apply for variable bounds or integrality restrictions of
1774 a scalar variable. For example:
1775
1776 ```jldoctest variable_in_set_ref_docstring
1777 julia> model = Model();
1778
1779 julia> @variable(model, x >= 0, Int)
1780 x
1781
1782 julia> is_variable_in_set(x)
1783 false
1784 ```
1785
1786 Use instead [`is_integer`](@ref), [`is_binary`](@ref), [`has_lower_bound`](@ref),
1787 [`has_upper_bound`](@ref), and [`is_fixed`](@ref).
1788
1789 ```jldoctest variable_in_set_ref_docstring
1790 julia> model = Model();
1791
1792 julia> @variable(model, x >= 0, Int)
1793 x
1794
1795 julia> is_integer(x)
1796 true
1797
1798 julia> has_lower_bound(x)
1799 true
1800 ```
1801
1802 ## Example
1803
1804 ```jldoctest
1805 julia> model = Model();
1806
1807 julia> @variable(model, x[1:2, 1:2], PSD)
1808 2×2 LinearAlgebra.Symmetric{VariableRef, Matrix{VariableRef}}:
1809 x[1,1] x[1,2]
1810 x[1,2] x[2,2]
1811
1812 julia> is_variable_in_set(x)
1813 true
1814
1815 julia> c = VariableInSetRef(x)
1816 [x[1,1] x[1,2]
1817 ⋯ x[2,2]] ∈ PSDCone()
1818
1819 julia> @variable(model, y)
1820 y
1821
1822 julia> is_variable_in_set(y)
1823 false
1824
1825 julia> @variable(model, z in Semicontinuous(1, 2))
1826 z
1827
1828 julia> is_variable_in_set(z)
1829 true
1830
1831 julia> c_z = VariableInSetRef(z)
1832 z ∈ MathOptInterface.Semicontinuous{Int64}(1, 2)
1833 ```
1834 """
1835 function is_variable_in_set(x::AbstractJuMPScalar)
1836 model = owner_model(x)
1837 return haskey(model.variable_in_set_ref, x)
1838 end
1839
1840 function is_variable_in_set(x::AbstractArray{<:AbstractJuMPScalar})
1841 model = owner_model(first(x))
1842 return haskey(model.variable_in_set_ref, x)
1843 end
1844
1845 """
1846 VariableInSetRef(
1847 model::GenericModel,
1848 x::Union{AbstractJuMPScalar,AbstractArray{<:AbstractJuMPScalar}},
1849 )
1850
1851 Return the constraint reference associated with `x` when it is constrained on
1852 creation.
1853
1854 A variable is constrained on creation if it uses the `x in S` or `x, set = S`
1855 syntax in the [`@variable`](@ref) macro.
1856
1857 This function errors if `x` was not constrained on creation. To check if the
1858 variable was constrained on creation, use [`is_variable_in_set`](@ref).
1859
1860 ## Exceptions
1861
1862 This function does not apply for variable bounds or integrality restrictions of
1863 a scalar variable. For example:
1864
1865 ```jldoctest variable_in_set_ref_docstring
1866 julia> model = Model();
1867
1868 julia> @variable(model, x >= 0, Int)
1869 x
1870
1871 julia> is_variable_in_set(x)
1872 false
1873 ```
1874
1875 Use instead [`IntegerRef`](@ref), [`BinaryRef`](@ref), [`LowerBoundRef`](@ref),
1876 [`UpperBoundRef`](@ref), and [`FixRef`](@ref).
1877
1878 ```jldoctest variable_in_set_ref_docstring
1879 julia> model = Model();
1880
1881 julia> @variable(model, x >= 0, Int)
1882 x
1883
1884 julia> IntegerRef(x)
1885 x integer
1886
1887 julia> LowerBoundRef(x)
1888 x ≥ 0
1889 ```
1890
1891 ## Example
1892
1893 ```jldoctest
1894 julia> model = Model();
1895
1896 julia> @variable(model, x[1:2, 1:2], PSD)
1897 2×2 LinearAlgebra.Symmetric{VariableRef, Matrix{VariableRef}}:
1898 x[1,1] x[1,2]
1899 x[1,2] x[2,2]
1900
1901 julia> is_variable_in_set(x)
1902 true
1903
1904 julia> c = VariableInSetRef(x)
1905 [x[1,1] x[1,2]
1906 ⋯ x[2,2]] ∈ PSDCone()
1907
1908 julia> @variable(model, y)
1909 y
1910
1911 julia> is_variable_in_set(y)
1912 false
1913
1914 julia> @variable(model, z in Semicontinuous(1, 2))
1915 z
1916
1917 julia> is_variable_in_set(z)
1918 true
1919
1920 julia> c_z = VariableInSetRef(z)
1921 z ∈ MathOptInterface.Semicontinuous{Int64}(1, 2)
1922 ```
1923 """
1924 function VariableInSetRef(x::AbstractJuMPScalar)
1925 model = owner_model(x)
1926 ci = get(model.variable_in_set_ref, x, nothing)
1927 if ci === nothing
1928 error("`VariableInSetRef` does not exist for `$x`")
1929 end
1930 return constraint_ref_with_index(model, ci)
1931 end
1932
1933 function VariableInSetRef(x::AbstractArray{<:AbstractJuMPScalar})
1934 model = owner_model(first(x))
1935 ci = get(model.variable_in_set_ref, x, nothing)
1936 if ci === nothing
1937 error("`VariableInSetRef` does not exist for `$x`")
1938 end
1939 return constraint_ref_with_index(model, ci)
1940 end

2288 VariableConstrainedOnCreation <: AbstractVariable

2291
2292 Adding this variable can be understood as doing:
2293 ```julia
2294 function JuMP.add_variable(
2295 model::GenericModel,
2296 variable::VariableConstrainedOnCreation,
2297 names,
2298 )
2299 var_ref = add_variable(model, variable.scalar_variable, name)
2300 add_constraint(model, VectorConstraint(var_ref, variable.set))
2301 return var_ref
2302 end
2303 ```
2304 but adds the variables with `MOI.add_constrained_variable(model, variable.set)`
2305 instead.
2306 """
2307 struct VariableConstrainedOnCreation{
2308 S<:MOI.AbstractScalarSet,
2309 ScalarVarType<:AbstractVariable,
2310 } <: AbstractVariable
2311 scalar_variable::ScalarVarType
2312 set::S
2313 end

2316 model::GenericModel{T},
2317 variable::VariableConstrainedOnCreation,
2318 name::String,
2319 ) where {T}
2320 x, ci = _moi_add_constrained_variable(
2321 backend(model),
2322 variable.scalar_variable,
2323 variable.set,
2324 name,
2325 T,
2326 )
2327 ret = GenericVariableRef(model, x)
2328 model.variable_in_set_ref[ret] = ci
2329 return ret

2347 var_index, con_index = MOI.add_constrained_variable(moi_backend, set)
2348 _moi_constrain_variable(moi_backend, var_index, scalar_variable.info, T)
2349 supports = MOI.supports(moi_backend, MOI.VariableName(), MOI.VariableIndex)
2350 if !isempty(name) && supports
2351 MOI.set(moi_backend, MOI.VariableName(), var_index, name)
2352 end
2353 return var_index, con_index
2354 end
2355
2356 """
2357 VariablesConstrainedOnCreation <: AbstractVariable
2358
2359 Vector of variables `scalar_variables` constrained to belong to `set`.
2360 Adding this variable can be thought as doing:
2361 ```julia
2362 function JuMP.add_variable(
2363 model::GenericModel,
2364 variable::VariablesConstrainedOnCreation,
2365 names,
2366 )
2367 v_names = vectorize(names, variable.shape)
2368 var_refs = add_variable.(model, variable.scalar_variables, v_names)
2369 add_constraint(model, VectorConstraint(var_refs, variable.set))
2370 return reshape_vector(var_refs, variable.shape)
2371 end
2372 ```
2373 but adds the variables with `MOI.add_constrained_variables(model, variable.set)`
2374 instead. See [the MOI documentation](https://jump.dev/MathOptInterface.jl/v0.9.3/apireference/#Variables-1)
2375 for the difference between adding the variables with `MOI.add_constrained_variables`
2376 and adding them with `MOI.add_variables` and adding the constraint separately.
2377 """
2378 struct VariablesConstrainedOnCreation{
2379 S<:MOI.AbstractVectorSet,
2380 Shape<:AbstractShape,
2381 ScalarVarType<:AbstractVariable,
2382 } <: AbstractVariable
2383 scalar_variables::Vector{ScalarVarType}
2384 set::S
2385 shape::Shape
2386 end
2387
2388 function VariablesConstrainedOnCreation(
2389 variables::Vector{<:AbstractVariable},
2390 set::MOI.AbstractVectorSet,
2391 )
2392 if length(variables) != MOI.dimension(set)
2393 throw(
2394 DimensionMismatch(
2395 "Unable to add variables constrained on creation: " *
2396 "the number of variables, $(length(variables)), does not " *
2397 "match the output dimension of the set, $(MOI.dimension(set)).",
2398 ),
2399 )
2400 end
2401 return VariablesConstrainedOnCreation(variables, set, VectorShape())
2402 end
2403
2404 function add_variable(
2405 model::GenericModel{T},
2406 variable::VariablesConstrainedOnCreation,
2407 names,
2408 ) where {T}
2409 x, ci = _moi_add_constrained_variables(
2410 backend(model),
2411 variable.scalar_variables,
2412 variable.set,
2413 vectorize(names, variable.shape),
2414 T,
2415 )
2416 ret = reshape_vector(GenericVariableRef{T}.(model, x), variable.shape)
2417 if ci !== nothing # ci === nothing if variable.set isa MOI.Reals
2418 model.variable_in_set_ref[ret] = ci
2419 if variable.shape != ScalarShape() && variable.shape != VectorShape()
2420 model.shapes[ci] = variable.shape
2421 end
2422 end
2423 return ret
2424 end
2425
2426 function _moi_add_constrained_variables(
2427 moi_backend::MOI.ModelLike,
2428 scalar_variables::Vector{<:ScalarVariable},
2429 set::MOI.AbstractVectorSet,
2430 names::Union{Vector{String},Nothing},
2431 ::Type{T},
2432 ) where {T}
2433 var_indices, con_index = MOI.add_constrained_variables(moi_backend, set)
2434 for (index, variable) in zip(var_indices, scalar_variables)
2435 _moi_constrain_variable(moi_backend, index, variable.info, T)
2436 end
2437 supports = MOI.supports(moi_backend, MOI.VariableName(), MOI.VariableIndex)
2438 if names !== nothing && supports
2439 for (var_index, name) in zip(var_indices, names)
2440 if !isempty(name)
2441 MOI.set(moi_backend, MOI.VariableName(), var_index, name)
2442 end
2443 end
2444 end
2445 return var_indices, con_index
2446 end
2447
2448 function _moi_add_constrained_variables(
2449 moi_backend::MOI.ModelLike,
2450 scalar_variables::Vector{<:ScalarVariable},
2451 set::MOI.Reals,
2452 names::Union{Vector{String},Nothing},
2453 ::Type{T},
2454 ) where {T}
2455 var_indices = MOI.add_variables(moi_backend, MOI.dimension(set))
2456 for (index, variable) in zip(var_indices, scalar_variables)
2457 _moi_constrain_variable(moi_backend, index, variable.info, T)
2458 end
2459 supports = MOI.supports(moi_backend, MOI.VariableName(), MOI.VariableIndex)
2460 if names !== nothing && supports
2461 for (var_index, name) in zip(var_indices, names)
2462 if !isempty(name)
2463 MOI.set(moi_backend, MOI.VariableName(), var_index, name)
2464 end
2465 end
2466 end
2467 return var_indices, nothing
2468 end
2469
2470 """
2471 ComplexPlane
2472
2473 Complex plane object that can be used to create a complex variable in the
2474 [`@variable`](@ref) macro.
2475
2476 ## Example
2477
2478 Consider the following example:
2479
2480 ```jldoctest
2481 julia> model = Model();
2482
2483 julia> @variable(model, x in ComplexPlane())
2484 real(x) + imag(x) im
2485
2486 julia> all_variables(model)
2487 2-element Vector{VariableRef}:
2488 real(x)
2489 imag(x)
2490 ```
2491
2492 We see in the output of the last command that two real variables were created.
2493 The Julia variable `x` binds to an affine expression in terms of these two
2494 variables that parametrize the complex plane.
2495 """
2496 struct ComplexPlane end
2497
2498 """
2499 ComplexVariable{S,T,U,V} <: AbstractVariable
2500
2501 A struct used when adding complex variables.
2502
2503 See also: [`ComplexPlane`](@ref).
2504 """
2505 struct ComplexVariable{S,T,U,V} <: AbstractVariable
2506 info::VariableInfo{S,T,U,V}
2507 end
2508
2509 function build_variable(error_fn::Function, v::ScalarVariable, ::ComplexPlane)
2510 if _is_binary(v) || _is_integer(v)
2511 # We would then need to fix the imaginary value to zero. Let's wait to
2512 # see if there is need for such complication first.
2513 error_fn(
2514 "Creation of binary or integer complex variable is not supported.",
2515 )
2516 end
2517 return ComplexVariable(v.info)
2518 end
2519
2520 function _mapinfo(f::Function, v::ScalarVariable)
2521 info = v.info
2522 return ScalarVariable(
2523 VariableInfo(
2524 info.has_lb,
2525 f(info.lower_bound),
2526 info.has_ub,
2527 f(info.upper_bound),
2528 info.has_fix,
2529 f(info.fixed_value),
2530 info.has_start,
2531 f(info.start),
2532 info.binary,
2533 info.integer,
2534 ),
2535 )
2536 end
2537
2538 function _real(s::String)
2539 if isempty(s)
2540 return s
2541 end
2542 return string("real(", s, ")")
2543 end
2544
2545 function _imag(s::String)
2546 if isempty(s)
2547 return s
2548 end
2549 return string("imag(", s, ")")
2550 end
2551
2552 _real(v::ScalarVariable) = _mapinfo(real, v)
2553
2554 _real(scalar) = real(scalar)
2555
2556 _imag(v::ScalarVariable) = _mapinfo(imag, v)
2557
2558 _imag(scalar) = imag(scalar)
2559
2560 _conj(v::ScalarVariable) = _mapinfo(conj, v)
2561
2562 function _isreal(v::ScalarVariable)
2563 return isreal(v.info.lower_bound) &&
2564 isreal(v.info.upper_bound) &&
2565 isreal(v.info.fixed_value) &&
2566 isreal(v.info.start)
2567 end
2568
2569 _is_binary(v::ScalarVariable) = v.info.binary
2570
2571 _is_integer(v::ScalarVariable) = v.info.integer
2572
2573 function add_variable(
2574 model::GenericModel{T},
2575 v::ComplexVariable,
2576 name::String = "",
2577 ) where {T}
2578 model.is_model_dirty = true
2579 var = ScalarVariable(v.info)
2580 real_part = add_variable(model, _real(var), _real(name))
2581 imag_part = add_variable(model, _imag(var), _imag(name))
2582 # Efficiently build `real_part + imag_part * im`
2583 return GenericAffExpr{Complex{T},GenericVariableRef{T}}(
2584 zero(Complex{T}),
2585 real_part => one(Complex{T}),
2586 imag_part => convert(Complex{T}, im),
2587 )
2588 end
2589
2590 function build_variable(
2591 error_fn::Function,
2592 variables::AbstractArray{<:ScalarVariable},
2593 set::ComplexPlane,
2594 )
2595 return build_variable.(error_fn, variables, Ref(set))
2596 end
2597
2598 function add_variable(
2599 model::GenericModel,
2600 variables::AbstractArray{<:ComplexVariable},
2601 name::Union{<:AbstractArray{String},String} = "",
2602 )
2603 return add_variable.(model, variables, name)
2604 end
2605
2606 """
2607 reduced_cost(x::GenericVariableRef{T})::T where {T}
2608
2609 Return the reduced cost associated with variable `x`.
2610
2611 One interpretation of the reduced cost is that it is the change in the objective
2612 from an infinitesimal relaxation of the variable bounds.
2613
2614 This method is equivalent to querying the shadow price of the active variable
2615 bound (if one exists and is active).
2616
2617 See also: [`shadow_price`](@ref).
2618
2619 ## Example
2620
2621 ```jldoctest
2622 julia> import HiGHS
2623
2624 julia> model = Model(HiGHS.Optimizer);
2625
2626 julia> set_silent(model)
2627
2628 julia> @variable(model, x <= 1);
2629
2630 julia> @objective(model, Max, 2 * x + 1);
2631
2632 julia> optimize!(model)
2633
2634 julia> dual_status(model)
2635 FEASIBLE_POINT::ResultStatusCode = 1
2636
2637 julia> reduced_cost(x)
2638 2.0
2639 ```
2640 """
2641 function reduced_cost(x::GenericVariableRef{T})::T where {T}
2642 model = owner_model(x)
2643 if !has_duals(model)
2644 error(
2645 "Unable to query reduced cost of variable because model does" *
2646 " not have duals available.",
2647 )
2648 end
2649 sign = objective_sense(model) == MIN_SENSE ? one(T) : -one(T)
2650 if is_fixed(x)
2651 return sign * dual(FixRef(x))
2652 end
2653 rc = 0.0
2654 if has_upper_bound(x)
2655 rc += dual(UpperBoundRef(x))
2656 end
2657 if has_lower_bound(x)
2658 rc += dual(LowerBoundRef(x))
2659 end
2660 return sign * rc
2661 end
2662
2663 """
2664 all_variables(model::GenericModel{T})::Vector{GenericVariableRef{T}} where {T}
2665
2666 Returns a list of all variables currently in the model. The variables are
2667 ordered by creation time.
2668
2669 ## Example
2670
2671 ```jldoctest
2672 julia> model = Model();
2673
2674 julia> @variable(model, x);
2675
2676 julia> @variable(model, y);
2677
2678 julia> all_variables(model)
2679 2-element Vector{VariableRef}:
2680 x
2681 y
2682 ```
2683 """
2684 function all_variables(model::GenericModel{T}) where {T}
2685 all_indices =
2686 MOI.get(model, MOI.ListOfVariableIndices())::Vector{MOI.VariableIndex}
2687 return GenericVariableRef{T}[
2688 GenericVariableRef(model, idx) for idx in all_indices
2689 ]
2690 end
2691
2692 function dual(::GenericVariableRef)
2693 return error(
2694 "To query the dual variables associated with a variable bound, first " *
2695 "obtain a constraint reference using one of `UpperBoundRef`, `LowerBoundRef`, " *
2696 "or `FixRef`, and then call `dual` on the returned constraint reference.\nFor " *
2697 "example, if `x <= 1`, instead of `dual(x)`, call `dual(UpperBoundRef(x))`.",
2698 )
2699 end
2700
2701 function value(var_value::Function, Q::AbstractArray{<:AbstractJuMPScalar})
2702 return value.(var_value, Q)
2703 end
2704
2705 function value(Q::AbstractArray{<:AbstractJuMPScalar}; result::Int = 1)
2706 return value.(Q; result)
2707 end
2708
2709 # Fallback. See JuMP#3775
2710 value(::_MA.Zero; result::Int = 1) = 0.0
2711
2712 value(x::Number; result::Int = 1) = x
2713
2714 value(::Function, x::Number) = x
2715
2716 function _info_from_variable(v::GenericVariableRef)
2717 has_lb = has_lower_bound(v)
2718 lb = has_lb ? lower_bound(v) : -Inf
2719 has_ub = has_upper_bound(v)
2720 ub = has_ub ? upper_bound(v) : Inf
2721 has_fix = is_fixed(v)
2722 fixed_value = has_fix ? fix_value(v) : NaN
2723 has_start, start = false, NaN
2724 if MOI.supports(
2725 backend(owner_model(v)),
2726 MOI.VariablePrimalStart(),
2727 MOI.VariableIndex,
2728 )
2729 start = start_value(v)
2730 has_start = start !== nothing
2731 end
2732 binary = is_binary(v)
2733 integer = is_integer(v)
2734 return VariableInfo(
2735 has_lb,
2736 lb,
2737 has_ub,
2738 ub,
2739 has_fix,
2740 fixed_value,
2741 has_start,
2742 start,
2743 binary,
2744 integer,
2745 )
2746 end
2747
2748 """
2749 relax_integrality(model::GenericModel)
2750
2751 Modifies `model` to "relax" all binary and integrality constraints on
2752 variables. Specifically,
2753
2754 - Binary constraints are deleted, and variable bounds are tightened if
2755 necessary to ensure the variable is constrained to the interval ``[0, 1]``.
2756 - Integrality constraints are deleted without modifying variable bounds.
2757 - An error is thrown if semi-continuous or semi-integer constraints are
2758 present (support may be added for these in the future).
2759 - All other constraints are ignored (left in place). This includes discrete
2760 constraints like SOS and indicator constraints.
2761
2762 Returns a function that can be called without any arguments to restore the
2763 original model. The behavior of this function is undefined if additional
2764 changes are made to the affected variables in the meantime.
2765
2766 ## Example
2767
2768 ```jldoctest
2769 julia> model = Model();
2770
2771 julia> @variable(model, x, Bin);
2772
2773 julia> @variable(model, 1 <= y <= 10, Int);
2774
2775 julia> @objective(model, Min, x + y);
2776
2777 julia> undo_relax = relax_integrality(model);
2778
2779 julia> print(model)
2780 Min x + y
2781 Subject to
2782 x ≥ 0
2783 y ≥ 1
2784 x ≤ 1
2785 y ≤ 10
2786
2787 julia> undo_relax()
2788
2789 julia> print(model)
2790 Min x + y
2791 Subject to
2792 y ≥ 1
2793 y ≤ 10
2794 y integer
2795 x binary
2796 ```
2797 """
2798 function relax_integrality(model::GenericModel)
2799 return _relax_or_fix_integrality(nothing, model)
2800 end
2801
2802 """
2803 fix_discrete_variables([var_value::Function = value,] model::GenericModel)
2804
2805 Modifies `model` to convert all binary and integer variables to continuous
2806 variables with fixed bounds of `var_value(x)`.
2807
2808 ## Return
2809
2810 Returns a function that can be called without any arguments to restore the
2811 original model. The behavior of this function is undefined if additional
2812 changes are made to the affected variables in the meantime.
2813
2814 ## Notes
2815
2816 - An error is thrown if semi-continuous or semi-integer constraints are
2817 present (support may be added for these in the future).
2818 - All other constraints are ignored (left in place). This includes discrete
2819 constraints like SOS and indicator constraints.
2820
2821 ## Example
2822
2823 ```jldoctest
2824 julia> model = Model();
2825
2826 julia> @variable(model, x, Bin, start = 1);
2827
2828 julia> @variable(model, 1 <= y <= 10, Int, start = 2);
2829
2830 julia> @objective(model, Min, x + y);
2831
2832 julia> undo_relax = fix_discrete_variables(start_value, model);
2833
2834 julia> print(model)
2835 Min x + y
2836 Subject to
2837 x = 1
2838 y = 2
2839
2840 julia> undo_relax()
2841
2842 julia> print(model)
2843 Min x + y
2844 Subject to
2845 y ≥ 1
2846 y ≤ 10
2847 y integer
2848 x binary
2849 ```
2850 """
2851 function fix_discrete_variables(var_value::Function, model::GenericModel)
2852 return _relax_or_fix_integrality(var_value, model)
2853 end
2854
2855 function fix_discrete_variables(model::GenericModel)
2856 return fix_discrete_variables(value, model)
2857 end
2858
2859 function _relax_or_fix_integrality(
2860 var_value::Union{Nothing,Function},
2861 model::GenericModel{T},
2862 ) where {T}
2863 if num_constraints(model, GenericVariableRef{T}, MOI.Semicontinuous{T}) > 0
2864 error(
2865 "Support for relaxing semicontinuous constraints is not " *
2866 "yet implemented.",
2867 )
2868 end
2869 if num_constraints(model, GenericVariableRef{T}, MOI.Semiinteger{T}) > 0
2870 error(
2871 "Support for relaxing semi-integer constraints is not " *
2872 "yet implemented.",
2873 )
2874 end
2875 discrete_variable_constraints = vcat(
2876 all_constraints(model, GenericVariableRef{T}, MOI.ZeroOne),
2877 all_constraints(model, GenericVariableRef{T}, MOI.Integer),
2878 )
2879 # We gather the info first because we cannot modify-then-query.
2880 info_pre_relaxation = map(discrete_variable_constraints) do c
2881 v = GenericVariableRef{T}(c)
2882 solution = var_value === nothing ? nothing : var_value(v)
2883 return (v, solution, _info_from_variable(v))
2884 end
2885 # Now we can modify.
2886 for (v, solution, info) in info_pre_relaxation
2887 if info.integer
2888 unset_integer(v)
2889 elseif info.binary
2890 unset_binary(v)
2891 if !info.has_fix
2892 set_lower_bound(v, max(zero(T), info.lower_bound))
2893 set_upper_bound(v, min(one(T), info.upper_bound))
2894 elseif info.fixed_value < 0 || info.fixed_value > 1
2895 error(
2896 "The model has no valid relaxation: binary variable " *
2897 "fixed out of bounds.",
2898 )
2899 end
2900 end
2901 if solution !== nothing
2902 fix(v, solution; force = true)
2903 end
2904 end
2905 function unrelax()
2906 for (v, solution, info) in info_pre_relaxation
2907 if solution !== nothing
2908 unfix(v)
2909 end
2910 if info.has_lb
2911 set_lower_bound(v, info.lower_bound)
2912 end
2913 if info.has_ub
2914 set_upper_bound(v, info.upper_bound)
2915 end
2916 if info.integer
2917 set_integer(v)
2918 end
2919 if info.binary
2920 set_binary(v)
2921 end
2922 # Now a special case: when binary variables are relaxed, we add
2923 # [0, 1] bounds, but only if the variable was not previously fixed
2924 # and we did not provide a fixed value, and a bound did not already
2925 # exist. In this case, delete the new bounds that we added.
2926 if solution === nothing && info.binary && !info.has_fix
2927 if !info.has_lb
2928 delete_lower_bound(v)
2929 end
2930 if !info.has_ub
2931 delete_upper_bound(v)
2932 end
2933 end
2934 end
2935 return
2936 end
2937 return unrelax
2938 end
2939
2940 """
2941 set_normalized_coefficient(
2942 constraint::ConstraintRef,
2943 variable::GenericVariableRef,
2944 value::Number,
2945 )
2946
2947 Set the coefficient of `variable` in the constraint `constraint` to `value`.
2948
2949 Note that prior to this step, JuMP will aggregate multiple terms containing the
2950 same variable. For example, given a constraint `2x + 3x <= 2`,
2951 `set_normalized_coefficient(con, x, 4)` will create the constraint `4x <= 2`.
2952
2953 ## Example
2954
2955 ```jldoctest; filter=r"≤|<="
2956 julia> model = Model();
2957
2958 julia> @variable(model, x)
2959 x
2960
2961 julia> @constraint(model, con, 2x + 3x <= 2)
2962 con : 5 x ≤ 2
2963
2964 julia> set_normalized_coefficient(con, x, 4)
2965
2966 julia> con
2967 con : 4 x ≤ 2
2968 ```
2969 """
2970 function set_normalized_coefficient(
2971 con_ref::ConstraintRef{<:AbstractModel,<:MOI.ConstraintIndex{F}},
2972 variable::AbstractVariableRef,
2973 value::Number,
2974 ) where {T,F<:Union{MOI.ScalarAffineFunction{T},MOI.ScalarQuadraticFunction{T}}}
2975 model = owner_model(con_ref)
2976 MOI.modify(
2977 backend(model),
2978 index(con_ref),
2979 MOI.ScalarCoefficientChange(index(variable), convert(T, value)),
2980 )
2981 model.is_model_dirty = true
2982 return
2983 end
2984
2985 """
2986 set_normalized_coefficient(
2987 constraints::AbstractVector{
2988 <:ConstraintRef{<:AbstractModel,<:MOI.ConstraintIndex{F}},
2989 },
2990 variables::AbstractVector{<:AbstractVariableRef},
2991 coeffs::AbstractVector{<:Number},
2992 ) where {
2993 T,
2994 F<:Union{MOI.ScalarAffineFunction{T},MOI.ScalarQuadraticFunction{T}},
2995 }
2996
2997 Set multiple coefficient of `variables` in the constraints `constraints` to
2998 `coeffs`.
2999
3000 ## Concrete types
3001
3002 Note that `constraints` must be a concrete vector of a single constraint type.
3003 You cannot mix, for example, `<=` and `>=` constraints in the same vector.
3004
3005 ## Normalization
3006
3007 Note that prior to this step, JuMP will aggregate multiple terms containing the
3008 same variable. For example, given a constraint `2x + 3x <= 2`,
3009 `set_normalized_coefficient(con, [x], [4])` will create the constraint `4x <= 2`.
3010
3011 ## Example
3012
3013 ```jldoctest; filter=r"≤|<="
3014 julia> model = Model();
3015
3016 julia> @variable(model, x)
3017 x
3018
3019 julia> @variable(model, y)
3020 y
3021
3022 julia> @constraint(model, con, 2x + 3x + 4y <= 2)
3023 con : 5 x + 4 y ≤ 2
3024
3025 julia> set_normalized_coefficient([con, con], [x, y], [6, 7])
3026
3027 julia> con
3028 con : 6 x + 7 y ≤ 2
3029 ```
3030 """
3031 function set_normalized_coefficient(
3032 constraints::AbstractVector{
3033 <:ConstraintRef{<:AbstractModel,<:MOI.ConstraintIndex{F}},
3034 },
3035 variables::AbstractVector{<:AbstractVariableRef},
3036 coeffs::AbstractVector{<:Number},
3037 ) where {T,F<:Union{MOI.ScalarAffineFunction{T},MOI.ScalarQuadraticFunction{T}}}
3038 c, n, m = length(constraints), length(variables), length(coeffs)
3039 if !(c == n == m)
3040 msg = "The number of constraints ($c), variables ($n) and coefficients ($m) must match"
3041 throw(DimensionMismatch(msg))
3042 end
3043 model = owner_model(first(constraints))
3044 MOI.modify(
3045 backend(model),
3046 index.(constraints),
3047 MOI.ScalarCoefficientChange.(index.(variables), convert.(T, coeffs)),
3048 )
3049 model.is_model_dirty = true
3050 return
3051 end
3052
3053 """
3054 set_normalized_coefficient(
3055 con_ref::ConstraintRef,
3056 variable::AbstractVariableRef,
3057 new_coefficients::Vector{Tuple{Int64,T}},
3058 )
3059
3060 Set the coefficients of `variable` in the constraint `con_ref` to
3061 `new_coefficients`, where each element in `new_coefficients` is a tuple which
3062 maps the row to a new coefficient.
3063
3064 Note that prior to this step, during constraint creation, JuMP will aggregate
3065 multiple terms containing the same variable.
3066
3067 ## Example
3068
3069 ```jldoctest; filter=r"≤|<="
3070 julia> model = Model();
3071
3072 julia> @variable(model, x)
3073 x
3074
3075 julia> @constraint(model, con, [2x + 3x, 4x] in MOI.Nonnegatives(2))
3076 con : [5 x, 4 x] ∈ MathOptInterface.Nonnegatives(2)
3077
3078 julia> set_normalized_coefficient(con, x, [(1, 2.0), (2, 5.0)])
3079
3080 julia> con
3081 con : [2 x, 5 x] ∈ MathOptInterface.Nonnegatives(2)
3082 ```
3083 """
3084 function set_normalized_coefficient(
3085 constraint::ConstraintRef{<:AbstractModel,<:MOI.ConstraintIndex{F}},
3086 variable::AbstractVariableRef,
3087 new_coefficients::Vector{Tuple{Int64,T}},
3088 ) where {T,F<:Union{MOI.VectorAffineFunction{T},MOI.VectorQuadraticFunction{T}}}
3089 model = owner_model(constraint)
3090 MOI.modify(
3091 backend(model),
3092 index(constraint),
3093 MOI.MultirowChange(index(variable), new_coefficients),
3094 )
3095 model.is_model_dirty = true
3096 return
3097 end
3098
3099 """
3100 set_normalized_coefficients(
3101 constraint::ConstraintRef{<:AbstractModel,<:MOI.ConstraintIndex{F}},
3102 variable::AbstractVariableRef,
3103 new_coefficients::Vector{Tuple{Int64,T}},
3104 ) where {T,F<:Union{MOI.VectorAffineFunction{T},MOI.VectorQuadraticFunction{T}}}
3105
3106 A deprecated method that now redirects to [`set_normalized_coefficient`](@ref).
3107 """
3108 function set_normalized_coefficients(
3109 constraint::ConstraintRef{<:AbstractModel,<:MOI.ConstraintIndex{F}},
3110 variable::AbstractVariableRef,
3111 new_coefficients::Vector{Tuple{Int64,T}},
3112 ) where {T,F<:Union{MOI.VectorAffineFunction{T},MOI.VectorQuadraticFunction{T}}}
3113 return set_normalized_coefficient(constraint, variable, new_coefficients)
3114 end
3115 """
3116 set_normalized_coefficient(
3117 constraint::ConstraintRef,
3118 variable_1:GenericVariableRef,
3119 variable_2:GenericVariableRef,
3120 value::Number,
3121 )
3122
3123 Set the quadratic coefficient associated with `variable_1` and `variable_2` in
3124 the constraint `constraint` to `value`.
3125
3126 Note that prior to this step, JuMP will aggregate multiple terms containing the
3127 same variable. For example, given a constraint `2x^2 + 3x^2 <= 2`,
3128 `set_normalized_coefficient(con, x, x, 4)` will create the constraint `4x^2 <= 2`.
3129
3130 ## Example
3131
3132 ```jldoctest; filter=r"≤|<="
3133 julia> model = Model();
3134
3135 julia> @variable(model, x[1:2]);
3136
3137 julia> @constraint(model, con, 2x[1]^2 + 3 * x[1] * x[2] + x[2] <= 2)
3138 con : 2 x[1]² + 3 x[1]*x[2] + x[2] ≤ 2
3139
3140 julia> set_normalized_coefficient(con, x[1], x[1], 4)
3141
3142 julia> set_normalized_coefficient(con, x[1], x[2], 5)
3143
3144 julia> con
3145 con : 4 x[1]² + 5 x[1]*x[2] + x[2] ≤ 2
3146 ```
3147 """
3148 function set_normalized_coefficient(
3149 constraint::ConstraintRef{<:AbstractModel,<:MOI.ConstraintIndex{F}},
3150 variable_1::AbstractVariableRef,
3151 variable_2::AbstractVariableRef,
3152 value::Number,
3153 ) where {T,F<:MOI.ScalarQuadraticFunction{T}}
3154 new_value = convert(T, value)
3155 if variable_1 == variable_2
3156 new_value *= T(2)
3157 end
3158 model = owner_model(constraint)
3159 MOI.modify(
3160 backend(model),
3161 index(constraint),
3162 MOI.ScalarQuadraticCoefficientChange(
3163 index(variable_1),
3164 index(variable_2),
3165 new_value,
3166 ),
3167 )
3168 model.is_model_dirty = true
3169 return
3170 end
3171
3172 """
3173 set_normalized_coefficient(
3174 constraints::AbstractVector{<:ConstraintRef},
3175 variables_1:AbstractVector{<:GenericVariableRef},
3176 variables_2:AbstractVector{<:GenericVariableRef},
3177 values::AbstractVector{<:Number},
3178 )
3179
3180 Set multiple quadratic coefficients associated with `variables_1` and
3181 `variables_2` in the constraints `constraints` to `values`.
3182
3183 Note that prior to this step, JuMP will aggregate multiple terms containing the
3184 same variable. For example, given a constraint `2x^2 + 3x^2 <= 2`,
3185 `set_normalized_coefficient(con, [x], [x], [4])` will create the constraint
3186 `4x^2 <= 2`.
3187
3188 ## Example
3189
3190 ```jldoctest; filter=r"≤|<="
3191 julia> model = Model();
3192
3193 julia> @variable(model, x[1:2]);
3194
3195 julia> @constraint(model, con, 2x[1]^2 + 3 * x[1] * x[2] + x[2] <= 2)
3196 con : 2 x[1]² + 3 x[1]*x[2] + x[2] ≤ 2
3197
3198 julia> set_normalized_coefficient([con, con], [x[1], x[1]], [x[1], x[2]], [4, 5])
3199
3200 julia> con
3201 con : 4 x[1]² + 5 x[1]*x[2] + x[2] ≤ 2
3202 ```
3203 """
3204 function set_normalized_coefficient(
3205 constraints::AbstractVector{
3206 <:ConstraintRef{<:AbstractModel,<:MOI.ConstraintIndex{F}},
3207 },
3208 variables_1::AbstractVector{<:AbstractVariableRef},
3209 variables_2::AbstractVector{<:AbstractVariableRef},
3210 coeffs::AbstractVector{<:Number},
3211 ) where {T,F<:MOI.ScalarQuadraticFunction{T}}
3212 c, m = length(constraints), length(coeffs)
3213 n1, n2 = length(variables_1), length(variables_1)
3214 if !(c == n1 == n2 == m)
3215 msg = "The number of constraints ($c), variables ($n1, $n2) and coefficients ($m) must match"
3216 throw(DimensionMismatch(msg))
3217 end
3218 new_coeffs = convert.(T, coeffs)
3219 for (i, x, y) in zip(eachindex(new_coeffs), variables_1, variables_2)
3220 if x == y
3221 new_coeffs[i] *= T(2)
3222 end
3223 end
3224 model = owner_model(first(constraints))
3225 MOI.modify(
3226 backend(model),
3227 index.(constraints),
3228 MOI.ScalarQuadraticCoefficientChange.(
3229 index.(variables_1),
3230 index.(variables_2),
3231 new_coeffs,
3232 ),
3233 )
3234 model.is_model_dirty = true
3235 return
3236 end
3237
3238 """
3239 normalized_coefficient(
3240 constraint::ConstraintRef,
3241 variable::GenericVariableRef,
3242 )
3243
3244 Return the coefficient associated with `variable` in `constraint` after JuMP has
3245 normalized the constraint into its standard form.
3246
3247 See also [`set_normalized_coefficient`](@ref).
3248
3249 ## Example
3250
3251 ```jldoctest; filter=r"≤|<="
3252 julia> model = Model();
3253
3254 julia> @variable(model, x)
3255 x
3256
3257 julia> @constraint(model, con, 2x + 3x <= 2)
3258 con : 5 x ≤ 2
3259
3260 julia> normalized_coefficient(con, x)
3261 5.0
3262
3263 julia> @constraint(model, con_vec, [x, 2x + 1, 3] >= 0)
3264 con_vec : [x, 2 x + 1, 3] ∈ Nonnegatives()
3265
3266 julia> normalized_coefficient(con_vec, x)
3267 2-element Vector{Tuple{Int64, Float64}}:
3268 (1, 1.0)
3269 (2, 2.0)
3270 ```
3271 """
3272 function normalized_coefficient(
3273 constraint::ConstraintRef{<:AbstractModel,MOI.ConstraintIndex{F,S}},
3274 variable::AbstractVariableRef,
3275 ) where {
3276 F<:Union{MOI.ScalarAffineFunction,MOI.ScalarQuadraticFunction},
3277 S<:MOI.AbstractScalarSet,
3278 }
3279 return coefficient(constraint_object(constraint).func, variable)
3280 end
3281
3282 function normalized_coefficient(
3283 constraint::ConstraintRef{<:AbstractModel,MOI.ConstraintIndex{F,S}},
3284 variable::AbstractVariableRef,
3285 ) where {
3286 F<:Union{MOI.VectorAffineFunction,MOI.VectorQuadraticFunction},
3287 S<:MOI.AbstractVectorSet,
3288 }
3289 c = coefficient.(constraint_object(constraint).func, variable)
3290 return filter!(!iszero ∘ last, collect(enumerate(c)))
3291 end
3292
3293 """
3294 normalized_coefficient(
3295 constraint::ConstraintRef,
3296 variable_1::GenericVariableRef,
3297 variable_2::GenericVariableRef,
3298 )
3299
3300 Return the quadratic coefficient associated with `variable_1` and `variable_2`
3301 in `constraint` after JuMP has normalized the constraint into its standard form.
3302
3303 See also [`set_normalized_coefficient`](@ref).
3304
3305 ## Example
3306
3307 ```jldoctest; filter=r"≤|<="
3308 julia> model = Model();
3309
3310 julia> @variable(model, x[1:2]);
3311
3312 julia> @constraint(model, con, 2x[1]^2 + 3 * x[1] * x[2] + x[2] <= 2)
3313 con : 2 x[1]² + 3 x[1]*x[2] + x[2] ≤ 2
3314
3315 julia> normalized_coefficient(con, x[1], x[1])
3316 2.0
3317
3318 julia> normalized_coefficient(con, x[1], x[2])
3319 3.0
3320
3321 julia> @constraint(model, con_vec, x.^2 <= [1, 2])
3322 con_vec : [x[1]² - 1, x[2]² - 2] ∈ Nonpositives()
3323
3324 julia> normalized_coefficient(con_vec, x[1], x[1])
3325 1-element Vector{Tuple{Int64, Float64}}:
3326 (1, 1.0)
3327
3328 julia> normalized_coefficient(con_vec, x[1], x[2])
3329 Tuple{Int64, Float64}[]
3330 ```
3331 """
3332 function normalized_coefficient(
3333 constraint::ConstraintRef{<:AbstractModel,MOI.ConstraintIndex{F,S}},
3334 variable_1::AbstractVariableRef,
3335 variable_2::AbstractVariableRef,
3336 ) where {F<:MOI.ScalarQuadraticFunction,S<:MOI.AbstractScalarSet}
3337 con = constraint_object(constraint)
3338 return coefficient(con.func, variable_1, variable_2)
3339 end
3340
3341 function normalized_coefficient(
3342 constraint::ConstraintRef{<:AbstractModel,MOI.ConstraintIndex{F,S}},
3343 variable_1::AbstractVariableRef,
3344 variable_2::AbstractVariableRef,
3345 ) where {F<:MOI.VectorQuadraticFunction,S<:MOI.AbstractVectorSet}
3346 f = constraint_object(constraint).func
3347 c = coefficient.(f, variable_1, variable_2)
3348 return filter!(!iszero ∘ last, collect(enumerate(c)))
3349 end
3350
3351 ###
3352 ### Error messages for common incorrect usages
3353 ###
3354
3355 function _logic_error_exception(sym::Symbol)
3356 return ErrorException(
3357 """
3358 Cannot evaluate `$(sym)` between a variable and a number.
3359
3360 There are three common mistakes that lead to this.
3361
3362 1. You tried to write a constraint that depends on the value of a variable, for
3363 example:
3364 ```julia
3365 model = Model()
3366 @variable(model, x[1:2])
3367 if x[1] $(sym) 1
3368 @constraint(model, x[2] == 0)
3369 end
3370 ```
3371 You cannot write a model like this. You must formulate your problem as a
3372 single optimization problem. Unfortunately, the way to do this is
3373 problem-specific and depends on your choice of solver. You may be able to
3374 use indicator constraints, or some other mixed-integer linear
3375 reformulation. If stuck, post your problem on the community forum:
3376 https://jump.dev/forum
3377
3378 2. You wrote a function that expected the value of a variable, but passed the
3379 variable instead. For example:
3380 ```julia
3381 foo(x) = x $(sym) 1 ? 0 : 1 - x
3382 model = Model()
3383 @variable(model, x)
3384 @expression(model, foo(x))
3385 ```
3386 To fix, create a nonlinear model with a user-defined operator:
3387 ```julia
3388 foo(x) = x $(sym) 1 ? 0 : 1 - x
3389 model = Model()
3390 @operator(model, op_f, 1, foo)
3391 @variable(model, x)
3392 @expression(model, op_f(x))
3393 ```
3394
3395 3. You tried to create a logical nonlinear expression outside a macro, for
3396 example:
3397 ```julia
3398 model = Model()
3399 @variable(model, x)
3400 expr = x $sym 1
3401 ```
3402 To fix, wrap the expression in the [`@expression`](@ref) macro:
3403 ```julia
3404 model = Model()
3405 @variable(model, x)
3406 expr = @expression(model, x $sym 1)
3407 ```
3408 """,
3409 )
3410 end
3411
3412 for sym in (:(<=), :(<))
3413 err = _logic_error_exception(sym)
3414 @eval begin
3415 Base.$(sym)(::GenericVariableRef, ::Number) = throw($err)
3416 Base.$(sym)(::Number, ::GenericVariableRef) = throw($err)
3417 end
3418 end
